{{Short description|Indian manufacturing company}} {{Orphan|date=April 2026}} {{Infobox company | name = PTC Industries Limited | type = [[Public company|Public]] | traded_as = {{BSE|539006}}
{{NSE|PTCIL}} | industry = [[Aerospace]], [[Manufacturing]] | founded = {{start date and age|1963}} | founder = Satish Agarwal | hq_location = Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India | area_served = Worldwide | key_people = Sachin Agarwal (Chairman and Managing Director) | products = Titanium and superalloy materials, precision castings, engineered components | subsidiaries = Aerolloy Technologies Limited | website = {{URL|https://www.ptcil.com/}} }} '''PTC Industries Limited''' is an Indian manufacturing company founded in 1963 and headquartered in [[Lucknow]], [[Uttar Pradesh]]. Apart from manufacturing cast components in stainless steel and higher alloys like duplex and super-duplex, it produces titanium and superalloy materials and castings for applications in aerospace, defence and industrial sectors.{{cite news |url=https://theprint.in/defence/indian-firm-sets-up-titanium-superalloy-plants-to-meet-global-need-safran-dassault-bae-line-up/2699217/ |title=Indian firm sets up titanium, superalloy plants to meet global need; Safran, Dassault, BAE line up |work=ThePrint |date=2025 |access-date=11 April 2026}} == History == === Founding and early development === PTC Industries was incorporated in 1963 as Precision Tools and Castings. The company started production as an investment casting foundry producing metal parts for industrial applications.{{cite news |url=https://www.forbesindia.com/article/hidden-gems/ptc-industries-casting-magic-with-metal/38258/1 |title=PTC Industries: Casting magic with metal |work=Forbes India |date=2014 |access-date=11 April 2026}} === Technology development === In 1998, the company licensed the Replicast process from Castings Technology International (CTI), a United Kingdom-based research organisation. Later, PTC Industries developed RapidCAST, a casting process for large and complex components, and expanded into ceramic moulding for single-piece castings. During this period, PTC's industrial customers included Rolls-Royce, Metso, Siemens and Flowserve. In 2014, ''Forbes India'' included the company in its list of "Hidden Gems", a group of fast-growing Indian companies. === Expansion into aerospace manufacturing === In 2017, PTC Industries established a titanium casting facility at its Advanced Manufacturing Technology Centre in Lucknow, with technical collaboration from CTI.{{cite journal |url=https://www.foundrymag.com/melt-pour/article/21931658/cti-helps-launch-indias-first-titanium-foundry |title=CTI Helps Launch India's First Titanium Foundry |journal=Foundry Management & Technology |date=October 2017 |access-date=11 April 2026}} The company manufactures titanium and superalloy materials and precision components for aerospace applications.{{cite news |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/lucknow/lucknow-firm-to-make-components-for-rafale-bae-system-safran/articleshow/87688790.cms |title=Lucknow firm to make components for Rafale, BAE System, Safran |work=The Times of India |date=November 2021 |access-date=11 April 2026}} === Strategic Materials Technology Complex === In May 2025, India's Defence Minister [[Rajnath Singh]] inaugurated the titanium and superalloy materials plant at the '''Strategic Materials Technology Complex (SMTC)''' in the Lucknow node of the [[Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor]]. The facility spans approximately 50 acres and produces titanium and superalloy materials.{{cite news |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/lucknow/worlds-largest-plant-to-produce-aerospace-grade-titanium-superalloy-materials-also-inaugurated/articleshow/121088146.cms |title=World's largest plant to produce aerospace-grade titanium, superalloy materials also inaugurated |work=The Times of India |date=May 2025 |access-date=11 April 2026}} Advanced metallurgical technologies including [[Vacuum arc remelting|Vacuum Arc Remelting]] (VAR), [[Plasma arc melting|Plasma Arc Melting]] (PAM), Electron Beam (EB) melting, and Vacuum Induction Melting (VIM) are being commissioned at this plant. In 2026, ''TIME'' and Statista included PTC Industries among India's fastest-growing companies.{{cite news |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/lucknow/ptc-industries-among-indias-top-100-fastest-growing-firms/articleshow/128622166.cms |title=PTC Industries among India's top 100 fastest-growing firms |work=The Times of India |date=2026 |access-date=11 April 2026}} == Operations and customers == The company supplies its products to international customers including [[Safran]], [[Dassault Aviation]], [[BAE Systems]], and [[Israel Aerospace Industries]]. == Subsidiary == '''Aerolloy Technologies Limited''' is a wholly owned subsidiary of PTC Industries that manufactures titanium and superalloy materials and components. In 2024, PTC Industries acquired UK-based Trac Precision Solutions, a manufacturer of aerospace components. == See also == * [[Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor]] * [[Make in India]] * [[Titanium alloy]] * [[Investment casting]] == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == * {{Official website|https://www.ptcil.com/}} [[Category:Manufacturing companies established in 1963]] [[Category:Companies based in Lucknow]] [[Category:Aerospace companies of India]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 1963]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Metal companies of India]]
